title: three-week-concentrated-alignment-brief-v0-1
content:
SYNOPSIS:

This is a working brief for a concentrated three-week alignment sprint to: 1) converge company-level OKR drafts for the upcoming quarter, 2) prepare an executive update that communicates tradeoffs and asks, and 3) produce a tight all-staff session that sets the operational tempo for the next 90 days. Treat as "notes-to-self" + shared working doc — not final.

OBJECTIVES FOR THE 3-WEEK SPRINT (high level):
- Converge on a single set of company OKRs by end of week 2 (leadership sign-off).
- Produce an exec update slide pack and 2-minute executive script (for board/exec sync).
- Ship a 40-minute all-staff with clear tactical asks, role-level commitments, and follow-up tasks.

PRINCIPLES/CONSTRAINTS:
- Keep the company-level OKRs to 4 objectives max. Prioritize clarity of expected outcomes and measurable KRs.
- Avoid tactical backlog capture at the company level — use "teams-level" commitments separately.
- Build the narrative: (problem -> what we will deliver -> measurable impact -> risks/mitigations).
- Be explicit about cross-team handoffs and support required from Eng Ops, Infra, and GTM.

DRAFT COMPANY OKRS (first-pass; action items inline):
Objective A: Make Redwood the predictable inference platform for production teams
- KR A1: Reduce median 95th percentile API tail latency for hosted text generation by 20% (baseline: 380ms -> target: 304ms) by end of quarter. (owner: eng-serving-runtime; action: kernel selection audit)
- KR A2: Achieve 99.95% uptime across hosted model endpoints for top-50 customers on reserved plan (owner: site-reliability-engineering)
- KR A3: Publish 5 curated performance profiles (model+hw+seqlen) and corresponding billing templates that lower per-token cost by 12% for targeted workloads (owner: product-hosted-api)

Objective B: Reduce unit cost for common customer workloads while preserving quality
- KR B1: Deploy two quantized model variants with validated quality delta <= 1.5% (per eval suite) for the top 3 open-source models (owner: applied-ml)
- KR B2: Ship caching+batching autopilot for on-hosted-routes and drive a 15% avg token cost reduction in pilot customers (owner: optimize)
- KR B3: Create a runway of recommended config profiles (small/medium/large) and document expected economics; 10 customers adopt by quarter-end (owner: developer-experience)

Objective C: Grow enterprise adoption of Dedicated and Private offerings
- KR C1: Close 3 committed Dedicated contracts (monthly+annual) with minimum ARR of $500k total (owner: go-to-market)
- KR C2: Achieve SOC2 readiness checklist completion and sign off on KMS/HSM integration for private offering (owner: security-and-compliance)
- KR C3: Reduce onboarding time for Private deployments from average 12 weeks to 6 weeks for pilot customers (owner: infra/private-deployments)

Objective D: Improve visibility and guardrails to prevent quality regressions
- KR D1: Roll out automated quality regression alerts tied to canonical prompt sets (coverage: 80% of top product flows)
- KR D2: Establish a weekly "eval release" cadence and a lightweight rollback playbook for model rollouts (owner: research/applied-ml + product)
- KR D3: Ship a per-route token+latency cost dashboard and have 5 product teams regularly use it in sprint planning

NOTES ON METRICS: baselines need validation — assigned owners should post baseline links (log snippets, dashboards) to the Confluence page by end of week 1.

EXECUTIVE UPDATE (one slide per block; 6 slides total recommended):
- Slide 1: One-line summary + top risk and top ask (so the board/exec know the single signal)
- Slide 2: OKRs and expected impact (headline numbers)
- Slide 3: Cost/backlog tradeoff (show 2 options and cost delta)
- Slide 4: Capacity and Dedicated pipeline (3 committed/outbound prospects)
- Slide 5: Security/compliance runway (SOC2, KMS, private infra)
- Slide 6: What we need from the execs (decisions + escalation paths)

Speaker notes: keep each slide to a 90–120 second narrative. For the top ask, be explicit (e.g., approve 3 FTEs for SRE sprint; approve $X runway for Dedicated pilot credits).

ALL‑STAFF AGENDA (40 minutes total):
- 0–5 min: Quick context (CEO) — where we are and why this matters
- 5–12 min: Product snapshot (product lead) — headline OKRs and what success looks like
- 12–22 min: Engineering highlight (serving runtime) — what we shipped, what is risky
- 22–30 min: Customer & GTM highlight — committed pilots and enterprise asks
- 30–36 min: People & ops (what we’re changing in process; expected tradeoffs)
- 36–40 min: Rapid-fire Q&A + micro-commitments (collect owners for follow-ups)

Deliverables for All‑Staff: 2–3 micro-asks for ICs (e.g., complete post-mortems for release X; volunteer for pilot support slots), and a single follow-up doc with role-level commitments to be published on Monday after the session.

COMMUNICATION PLAN:
- Week 0 (prep): Draft OKRs -> leadership sync -> publish initial narrative to Confluence (owner: product-ops)
- Week 1: Leadership review & iterate -> collect baseline metrics (owners assigned)
- Week 2: Exec slide pack finalization and rehearsal -> finalize all-staff agenda and speakers
- Week 3: All-staff + publish commitments -> open a 10-day feedback window for teams to annotate team-level commitments

RISKS & MITIGATION (quick list):
- Risk: Overloaded infra slows latency improvements. Mitigation: Reserve short-term burst capacity for experiments; prioritize kernel/compilation wins with lowest infra cost. Owner: infra/serving-runtime.
- Risk: Customers experience quality regressions with quantized models. Mitigation: staged rollout + automatic rollback + reconciliation tests in canary environment. Owner: applied-ml + sre.
- Risk: Leadership cannot converge on fewer objectives. Mitigation: reduce to 3 objectives with explicit criteria for what gets deferred; run an asymmetric decision: two execs have tie-break vote.

OPEN QUESTIONS (to resolve in week 1):
- Can we commit to the 20% latency improvement without additional headcount? If not, what budget ask is required?
- Which 3 models are the "top" models to prioritize for quantization? (marketing/field input needed)
- Is there appetite to move the Private deployment onboarding to a pre-built appliance (accelerates timeline but increases infra maintenance)?

QUICK WORKFLOW & ROLES (who does what this week):
- Elena Park: coordination, doc consolidation, all-staff run-of-show owner
- Marcus Nguyen: lead okr synthesis + run leadership sync (Thurs)
- Priya Nair: draft exec slide pack + speaker notes
- Jonah Reed: latency baseline collection + infra cost delta estimates
- Sofia Martinez: GTM input + Dedicated pipeline update

NEXT STEPS (this week):
- Owners post baselines and initial attachments in Confluence by Tue EOD.
- Leadership sync scheduled Wed 10:00–11:00 (calendar invite pending).
- Draft exec slide deck v0.1 due Fri; rehearsal next Tuesday.

NOTES TO SELF / WORKING BITS:
- Keep language simple for the all-staff — avoid engineering jargon.
- Pull 2 customer stories to punctuate the "why" — contact CS to nominate by Tue.
- Create a short feedback form after the all-staff (2 questions + optional comment) to capture friction points for teams.

APPENDIX (links and artefacts):
- Confluence page: confluence.company.com/display/COMPANY/Quarter+Alignment+Q2+2026
- Jira epic: REDWOOD-1983 (company-okrs-convergence)
- Draft slide deck (working): github/org/quarterly-deck/draft-v0.1

-- end of working brief --

(If you want, I can spin this into the exec slide pack skeleton and a separate all-staff run-of-show doc with speaker timings.)
